title: Normal intracranial anatomy: first session
author: NeuroImage example curriculum (unreviewed)
objective: Identify source-labelled regions in three MRI planes, relate them to 3D surfaces, preserve physical orientation and explain the limits of each source definition. Use these views as instructor-editable discussion material.

scenes.title: 1. Orientation and one shared location
scenes.prompt: Find the selected left caudate source label in all three MRI planes. Read its RAS coordinates and orientation markers. Toggle the radiological display convention and confirm that the physical coordinates and source side remain unchanged. Return to the recorded view before continuing.
scenes.note: The marker records a real voxel in the delivered left caudate label. It provides a reproducible source target for the shared 2D and 3D view.

scenes.title: 2. Deep structures in MRI and 3D
scenes.prompt: Identify the selected putamen, then inspect the separately delivered caudate and lateral ventricular labels. Describe their relative positions using the three planes and a rotated 3D view. Switch T1/T2 at the same cursor position. Which boundaries can you actually distinguish in the source images, and which depend on the parcellation?
scenes.note: Labels retain the source parcellation. Use the original MRI resolution and the source definition when assessing each labelled boundary.

scenes.title: 3. The represented ventricular spaces
scenes.prompt: Locate the third ventricular source label, then inspect the lateral and fourth ventricular labels in adjacent MRI sections. Explain which spaces the source distinguishes. Do not infer a complete connection, or its absence, from a small gap in a sampled label surface. Use Return to recorded view after exploring.
scenes.note: Selected ventricular spaces follow the source labels. Image sampling governs the visibility of thin connections; inspect adjacent sections for context.

scenes.title: 4. Precentral and postcentral source regions
scenes.prompt: Follow the selected precentral and neighboring postcentral source parcellations across slices and on their extracted surfaces. Describe the represented folds and their spatial relationship. Read the source definition before assigning a functional interpretation; these labels are not an individual functional map.
scenes.note: Cortical regions retain the source anatomical parcellation. Individual functional localization requires separate evidence.

scenes.title: 5. Brainstem source regions and ventricular context
scenes.prompt: Inspect the delivered Pons label and fourth ventricular label in sagittal, axial and coronal views. Compare their spatial relationship and follow adjacent source sections. Read the source metadata definition, 'unsegmented region of pons', to understand the represented extent. Record observations or definition questions in a teaching note.
scenes.note: The source display name is 'Pons'; its metadata definition is 'unsegmented region of pons'. Interpret the rendered extent using this documented source definition.

scenes.title: 6. Cerebellar source unions and coverage
scenes.prompt: Compare the two delivered cerebellar parcellation unions with MRI and the fourth ventricular source label. Inspect adjacent slices and rotate the scene. Explain what a union combines, which expected source values are absent, and why this does not establish complete folial, nuclear or individual variation coverage.
scenes.note: The displayed union combines the explicitly listed delivered parcellations. Source-value coverage is partial; detailed folial and nuclear representation is a separate source-development item.
